uforskammet.explanation: "Uforskammet" means "rude". To say a price is shockingly high, put it before the price word: "uforskammet dyrt" (outrageously expensive).

uforudsigelig.explanation: "Uforudsigelig" means "unpredictable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "forudsigelig" (predictable).

ugen efter.explanation: "Ugen efter" means "the week after". To say something happened in the week after a party: "Ugen efter festen var jeg syg" (The week after the party I was sick). For the day after, use "dagen efter": "Dagen efter rejste hun" (The day after, she left).

ugevis.explanation: "Ugevis" means "for weeks". It is built from "en uge" (a week) and the ending "-vis", which gives the meaning "week after week". To say you waited a long time: "Vi ventede ugevis" (We waited for weeks).

ugift.explanation: "Ugift" means "unmarried". It is built from "u-" (not) and "gift" (married). The same "u-" is in "uvenlig" (unfriendly), the opposite of "venlig" (friendly).

ugyldig.explanation: "Ugyldig" means "invalid". It is built from "u-" (not) and "gyldig" (valid). To say a code cannot be used: "Koden er ugyldig" (The code is invalid).

uheldig.explanation: "Uheldig" means "unlucky". It is built from "u-" (not) and "heldig" (lucky). When something turns out badly, it means "unfortunate": "en uheldig bemærkning" (an unfortunate remark).

uhyggelig.explanation: "Uhyggelig" means "creepy". It is built from "u-" (not) and "hyggelig" (cozy). To say a place gives you the creeps: "Huset er uhyggeligt" (The house is creepy).

uhyre.explanation: "Uhyre" means "immensely". To make an adjective stronger, put it before the adjective: "uhyre vigtig" (immensely important). As a noun, it takes "et" and means a monster: "et uhyre" (a monster).

uhøflig.explanation: "Uhøflig" means "rude". It is built from "u-" (not) and "høflig" (polite). To say who someone is rude to, add "mod" (to): "Vær ikke uhøflig mod din lærer" (Do not be rude to your teacher).

ukendt.explanation: "Ukendt" means "unknown". It is built from "u-" (not) and "kendt" (known). To say you do not know someone: "Han er ukendt for mig" (He is unknown to me).

ukraine.explanation: "Ukraine" means "Ukraine". To say where you are, use "i" (in): "Jeg bor i Ukraine" (I live in Ukraine). To say where you go, use "til" (to): "Vi rejser til Ukraine" (We travel to Ukraine).

ukrainsk.explanation: "Ukrainsk" means "Ukrainian". It is built from "Ukraine" (Ukraine) and the ending "-sk". English writes "Ukrainian" starting with U, but Danish writes "ukrainsk" starting with u.

ukrudt.explanation: "Ukrudt" means "weeds". This word has no article, so leave out "et": "Der er meget ukrudt i haven" (There are a lot of weeds in the garden).

uld.explanation: "Uld" means "wool". This word has no article. To say what something is made of, use "af" (of): "Sokkerne er af uld" (The socks are made of wool).

ulige.explanation: "Ulige" means "odd", as in an odd number such as 3 or 7. It is built from "u-" (not) and "lige" (even). For a different use, it means "unequal": "en ulige kamp" (an unequal fight).

ulovlig.explanation: "Ulovlig" means "illegal". It is built from "u-" (not) and "lovlig" (legal). To say the law forbids something: "Det er ulovligt at parkere her" (It is illegal to park here).

ultimativ.explanation: "Ultimativ" means "ultimate", as in the best or most extreme of its kind. It also means "final", as in a demand that leaves no room to negotiate: "et ultimativt krav" (a final demand).

ulydig.explanation: "Ulydig" means "disobedient". It is built from "u-" (not) and "lydig" (obedient).

ulykkelig.explanation: "Ulykkelig" means "unhappy". It is built from "u-" (not) and "lykkelig" (happy). To say someone is unhappy because of an event: "Han er ulykkelig efter bruddet" (He is unhappy after the breakup).

ulækker.explanation: "Ulækker" means "disgusting". Its opposite is "lækker" (tasty, nice): "Kagen er lækker" (The cake is tasty).

umiddelbart.explanation: "Umiddelbart" means "at first sight", before you look closer. When you put it in front of "efter" (after), it means "right": "umiddelbart efter mødet" (right after the meeting).

umoden.explanation: "Umoden" means "immature". It is built from "u-" (not) and "moden" (ripe, grown-up). For fruit that is not ready to eat, it means "unripe": "et umodent æble" (an unripe apple).

umulig.explanation: "Umulig" means "impossible". It is built from "u-" (not) and "mulig" (possible). When you say a person is hard to deal with, it also means "impossible" in that sense: "Du er umulig!" (You are impossible!)
